label.ta: Exercise 1.1 · Q1-i · English only; Tamil pending

q.en: Find the adjoint of the following: (i) [[−3, 4; 6, 2]]

steps.en: The adjoint is the transpose of the cofactor matrix. Each cofactor uses the determinant left after deleting its row and column, with alternating signs.
Delete row 1 and column 1; apply the cofactor sign.
Delete row 1 and column 2; apply the cofactor sign.
Delete row 2 and column 1; apply the cofactor sign.
Delete row 2 and column 2; apply the cofactor sign.
Transpose: row i of the cofactor matrix becomes column i of the adjoint.
Independent check: multiplication in both orders gives the determinant times the identity.

label.ta: Exercise 1.1 · Q2-i · English only; Tamil pending

q.en: Find the inverse (if it exists) of the following: (i) [[−2, 4; 1, −3]]

steps.en: An inverse exists exactly when the determinant is nonzero.
Expand along the first row, using signed cofactors.
Compute cofactor C11 by deleting row 1 and column 1.
Compute cofactor C12 by deleting row 1 and column 2.
Compute cofactor C21 by deleting row 2 and column 1.
Compute cofactor C22 by deleting row 2 and column 2.
Transpose the cofactors and divide each entry by the determinant.
Verify by multiplying in both orders; this also checks every entry of the inverse.

label.ta: Exercise 1.1 · Q3 · English only; Tamil pending

q.en: If F(α) = [[cos α, 0, sin α; 0, 1, 0; −sin α, 0, cos α]], show that [F(α)]⁻¹ = F(−α).

steps.en: Use cosine evenness and sine oddness to write the proposed inverse.
steps.eq: F(−α) = [[cos α, 0, −sin α; 0, 1, 0; sin α, 0, cos α]]

steps.en: Multiply row by column. The corner diagonal entries are cos²α + sin²α = 1; the off-diagonal corner entries cancel. The middle row and column give 1 on the diagonal and zeros elsewhere.
steps.eq: (1,1) = (3,3) = cos²α+sin²α = 1; (1,3) = −cos α sin α+sin α cos α = 0; (3,1) = −sin α cos α+cos α sin α = 0; F(α)F(−α) = I₃

steps.en: Reversing the factors changes only the signs of the cancelling terms, so the reverse product is also I₃. This proves the inverse for every real α.

label.ta: Exercise 1.1 · Q4 · English only; Tamil pending

q.en: If A = [[5, 3; −1, −2]], show that A² − 3A − 7I₂ = O₂. Hence find A⁻¹.

steps.en: Multiply A by itself, taking row-column dot products.
Subtract 3A and 7I₂ entry by entry.
Rearrange the identity as a product equal to I₂. Since A commutes with A−3I₂, the factor is both a left and a right inverse.
Subtract 3 from each diagonal entry, then divide all entries by 7.

label.ta: Exercise 1.1 · Q5 · English only; Tamil pending

steps.en: Write A = M/9. To prove the result, check that the rows and columns of M have squared length 81 and are mutually perpendicular.
Row squared lengths are 64+1+16, 16+16+49 and 1+64+16. Each is 81. Pairwise dot products vanish.
Column squared lengths are also 81. Their pairwise products are −8+16−8, −32+28+4 and 4+28−32, all zero.
The factor 1/9 occurs twice in each product, cancelling 81. Hence the transpose is the inverse.

steps.en: Let J = adj A. For a 3×3 matrix, det J = (det A)². Expand det J along the first row.
The identity adj(adj A) = |A|A gives A once each possible sign is considered.
Divide by +4 or −4. Both signs are possible because adj(−A) = adj A for order 3. No assumption in the question chooses one sign.
Verify both candidates by their cofactors, independently of the determinant identity.

records.answer: A = ±[[6, 2, 1; 5, 2, 2; 6, 2, 3]] (both signs satisfy the given adjoint).

label.ta: Exercise 1.1 · Q11 · English only; Tamil pending

q.en: A = [[1, tan x; −tan x, 1]], show that AᵀA⁻¹ = [[cos 2x, −sin 2x; sin 2x, cos 2x]].

steps.en: Work on the domain cos x ≠ 0, where the given tan x is defined. Put t = tan x. The determinant 1+t² is positive.
Multiply the two identical numerator matrices.
Divide the double-angle formulas by cos²x, which is nonzero on the stated domain.
Substitute these identities in all four positions.

records.answer: AᵀA⁻¹ = [[cos 2x, −sin 2x; sin 2x, cos 2x]], for cos x ≠ 0.

steps.en: Write the equation as AB = C. Since |B| = −10+3 = −7 ≠ 0, multiply on the right by B⁻¹; order matters.

Substitute the result into the original equation.

q.en: Decrypt the received encoded message [[2, −3]][[20, 4]] with the encryption matrix [[−1, −1; 2, 1]] and the decryption matrix as its inverse, where the system of codes are described by the numbers 1-26 to the letters A–Z respectively, and the number 0 to a blank space.

steps.en: The message is grouped into row vectors, so decrypt by multiplying each row on the right by the inverse of the encryption matrix.
Decode the first row with row-column dot products.
Decode the second row in the same order.
Map the numbers back to letters in sequence. Re-encrypting [8,5] and [12,16] returns the original rows.
